why: The plan is the right one for this copy: it makes a new int array the same size as data2 and copies every element in a loop, but it writes data2.length() twice, which is the documented ArrayHasLengthMethod misconception, so the code won't compile and this is an L2 answer with an error.

concepts.why: Using new to make a separate int array sized to the original is right, but the size expression data2.length() won't compile.
The answer says nothing about the int type itself.
The loop is only used as part of the traversal; nothing is said about for-loop rules.
i++ is only used as the usual loop update, with no claim about it.
Nothing is said about primitive types.

concepts.quote: int[] copy = new int[data2.length()]; for (int i = 0; i < data2.length(); i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: It creates the second array first and then copies each data2[i] into copy[i], which is the right plan, but the length() calls stop it from compiling.
The loop control is the standard pattern, with no reasoning given about it.

concepts.quote: for (int i = 0; i < data2.length(); i++) copy[i] = data2[i];
concepts.why: Going from i = 0 while i is less than the length visits every valid index, but the bound is written with length() instead of the length field.
It calls length() on an array, but an array's size is the field data2.length, written without parentheses.
